artists.biography:
Garbage is an alternative rock band formed in Madison, Wisconsin, in 1994. The group consists of Scottish singer Shirley Manson (vocals, guitar) and American musicians Duke Erikson (bass, guitar, keyboards, percussion), Steve Marker (guitar, keyboards) and Butch Vig (drums, percussion). All four members are involved in songwriting and production. The band have counted worldwide album sales of over 17 million units.

Garbage released a string of increasingly successful singles in 1995-1996, including "Stupid Girl" and "Only Happy When It Rains". Their debut album, Garbage, was an unexpected smash, selling over 4 million copies and certified double platinum in the UK, USA and Australia. Garbage won the Breakthrough Artist award at the 1996 MTV Europe Music Awards.

Garbage spent two years working on follow-up album, Version 2.0, which topped the charts in the UK upon its 1998 release and the following year was nominated for two Grammy Awards, Album of the Year and Best Rock Album. Version 2.0 went on to match the sales of its predecessor. Garbage followed this up by performing and co-producing the theme song to the nineteenth James Bond movie The World Is Not Enough.

Despite being named one of Rolling Stone's Top 10 Albums of the Year, Garbage's 2001 third album Beautiful Garbage failed to match the commercial success achieved by its predecessors. Garbage quietly disbanded in late 2003, but regrouped to complete fourth album Bleed Like Me in 2005, peaking at a career-high #4 in the U.S. The band cut short their concert tour in support of Bleed Like Me announcing an "indefinite hiatus", emphasizing that they had not broken up, but wished to pursue personal interests.
In 2006, Vig returned to producing while Manson worked on an as yet unreleased solo album. Garbage ended their hiatus in 2007 and released greatest hits retrospective Absolute Garbage. The band began work on their fifth studio album in October 2010. Not Your Kind of People was released on May 14, 2012 via the band's own independent label, Stunvolume Records.

Beautiful Garbage is the third studio album by Garbage, released on October 1, 2001. The album marked a significant stylistic departure from the band's first two releases, showcasing expanded musical variety that blended rock with electronica, new wave, hip hop, and girl group influences. The record featured stronger melodies and more direct lyrics compared to their previous work, demonstrating the band's evolution as songwriters and arrangers.

The album's creation process was notably documented in real-time, with lead singer Shirley Manson chronicling the band's weekly recording efforts online—making her one of the first high-profile musicians to maintain an Internet blog. This transparency into the creative process reflected the band's engagement with emerging digital culture at the turn of the millennium. The album was released across multiple formats in different territories, including a specially packaged limited edition CD in the United Kingdom featuring a distinctive rose-shaped holder.

Following its release, Garbage supported the album with an in-store performance at Chicago's Virgin Megastore on October 2, 2001, and subsequently served as the opening act for U2's Elevation Tour from mid-October through late October 2001. The album's commercial and critical standing was reinforced by its longevity in the band's catalog, with a remastered and expanded 20th anniversary edition released in 2021 that included two bonus CDs of b-sides, alternate versions, previously unreleased recordings, and remixes.
